stability.description: Controls how stable the generated voice is between each generation, between 0 (more varied/higher emotional range) and 1 (more stable/less emotional range).

similarityBoost.description: Controls how close the generated voice is to the original speaker, between 0 (more varied) and 1 (more similar).

speed.description: Controls the speed of the spoken voice as a multiplier, between 0.7 (slower) and 1.2 (faster).

PronunciationEntry.description:
One word or phrase and how to say it. The persona speaks the pronunciation in place of the text; captions and transcripts keep the original text.

Text and pronunciation must not be blank or contain `[` or `]`. Two entries can't have the same text (ignoring case and spacing) unless both set `caseSensitive` and differ only in case.

text.description: Word or phrase to replace, at most 100 Unicode characters.

kind.description:
- `sounds_like`: `pronunciation` is a respelling, such as `annum`. Works with every voice.
- `ipa`: `pronunciation` is Cartesia IPA markup, such as `<<ˈ|ɑ|n|ə|m>>`. Voices whose model reads IPA (Cartesia Sonic 3, ElevenLabs v3 and v4) speak it; other voices speak `soundsLike`, or leave the text unchanged without it.

pronunciation.description: How to say the text, at most 200 Unicode characters. A sounds-like respelling can't contain `<<` or `>>`.

soundsLike.description: IPA entries only. Respelling spoken by voices whose model can't read IPA.

caseSensitive.description: Match the text only with the same capitalization.

id.description: Pronunciation dictionary ID. Pass it as `voiceGenerationOptions.pronunciationDictionaryId` when creating a session token.

revision.description: Starts at 1 and increases with every save. Send it as `expectedRevision` to reject a write if someone else saved first.

code.description: Set when the saved entries, not the request, fail the current rules

row.description: One-based entry number, or null for an error outside an entry

field.description: Field with the error, or null for the whole entry or request

CreateMeetingInviteRequest.description: Request body for inviting a persona to a meeting.

meetingUrl.description: Google Meet, Zoom, or Microsoft Teams URL to join. URLs without a scheme are normalized to `https://`.

displayName.description: Optional display name for the meeting participant. The API appends an AI disclosure suffix when one is not already present.

region.description: Region the persona joins the call from. Pick the region closest to the meeting's participants. When omitted, a region is selected automatically from the requester's location.

regionPolicy.description: How strictly to honor the selected region. `preferred` may serve the invite from another region when the selected region has no capacity or is not currently offered; `strict` never leaves the selected region and returns a capacity error instead. `strict` requires an explicit `region`.

joinAt.description: When the persona should join the meeting (ISO 8601 with timezone). Must be in the future and no more than 7 days ahead. Scheduling at least 10 minutes ahead reserves the persona a guaranteed place on the call; shorter lead times join on time but use on-demand capacity and can be rejected at busy moments. When omitted, the persona joins immediately.

groupCall.description: Group-call turn-taking. When true (the default) the persona joins silently and only responds when addressed by its display name. Set to false for 1:1 conversations over the meeting infrastructure — the persona then greets on join and responds to everything it hears, like a regular session.

Audio passthrough (`enableAudioPassthrough: true` or `type: "audio_passthrough"`) is also rejected because the meeting bot has no external audio input. `personaPreset` is not a voice source for meeting invites; a persona with no voice cannot join. This object cannot include `personaId`.

imageUrl.description: Still image of the avatar, framed exactly like `videoUrl`, `idleVideoUrl` and a landscape session (the default). Use it as the thumbnail, poster or loading image wherever a preview video or the live stream replaces it, and give the image and the video the same box, `object-fit` and `object-position` so the avatar doesn't move when they swap. For Cara 4 avatars this is the 1152x768 landscape crop (the same image as `landscapeImageUrl`). Cara 4 avatars used to return their square source image here; that image is now `sourceImageUrl`. Empty when the avatar has no image yet.

sourceImageUrl.description: The image the avatar was created from. For Cara 4 avatars it is square (1152x1152) and shows more of the scene than the 1152x768 crop that preview videos and sessions use, so the avatar appears to zoom in when a video or call replaces it. Don't use it as a thumbnail, poster or loading image next to `videoUrl` or a session; use `imageUrl`, `landscapeImageUrl` or `portraitImageUrl`. For legacy avatars it is the same landscape image as `imageUrl`.

landscapeImageUrl.description: Still image cropped exactly as the engine frames landscape (1152x768) output, which is also the framing of `videoUrl` and `idleVideoUrl`. Use it with landscape sessions (the default) and preview videos. For avatars with legacy landscape source images this is the source image.

portraitImageUrl.description: Still image cropped exactly as the engine frames portrait (768x1152) output. Use it as the poster for a session started with portrait `videoWidth`/`videoHeight`. Preview videos are landscape, so don't swap this image for `videoUrl`. `null` when the avatar cannot render portrait output.

videoUrl.description: Signed URL for a verified muted MP4 preview of the avatar. Uses the idle loop if the talking preview is unavailable. Landscape (1152x768 for Cara 4 avatars, 720x480 for legacy avatars) and framed exactly like `imageUrl`, so pair it with `imageUrl` or `landscapeImageUrl`, not `sourceImageUrl`. The URL expires after 1 hour; re-fetch the avatar to get a fresh URL. `null` when the preview is unavailable or still generating.

idleVideoUrl.description: Signed URL for a muted idling-loop MP4 of the avatar, if one exists. Landscape and framed exactly like `imageUrl`, like `videoUrl`. The URL expires after 1 hour; re-fetch the avatar to get a fresh URL. `null` when unavailable or still generating.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the avatar was created.

requestBody.description:
Configuration for the session to be created. Supply `personaConfig.personaId` to use a persona you've already created (stateful), or the set `avatarId`/`voiceId`/`llmId`/`systemPrompt` to configure the persona at run time (ephemeral).

The returned token is valid for one hour and bound to this exact config.

Server-side SDKs in a secure context can skip this exchange and start a session directly by calling `POST /v1/engine/session` with their API key and the same configuration in the request body.

clientLabel.description: The client label for the session

personaConfig.description: Persona configuration. An avatar-only config (avatarId without voiceId and without enableAudioPassthrough: true) is only accepted together with a LiveKit, Agora or ElevenLabs Agent integration `environment`; on the default Anam WebRTC transport send an ephemeral config with voiceId and llmId (llmId "CUSTOMER_CLIENT_V1" for a client-side LLM) or set enableAudioPassthrough to true. Otherwise the request fails with 400 `avatar_only_requires_integration`.

avatarModel.description: Avatar model version. `cara-4` is pinned to a stable checkpoint; `cara-4-latest` tracks the newest Cara 4 checkpoint and may change between sessions.

uninterruptibleGreeting.description: When true, the greeting message cannot be interrupted by the user.

initialMessage.description: Custom first message the persona speaks to open the conversation. If empty or not provided, the persona generates its own greeting.
initialMessage.example: Hi there! I'm excited to chat with you today.

languageCode.description: Supported ISO 639 language code override (including "yue" for Cantonese) for transcription, replaces organisation level settings and multilingual (default) mode.

voiceGenerationOptions.description: Configuration options for voice generation, plus an optional pronunciation dictionary for this session.

directorNotes.description: Per-session performance overrides for the avatar. Only applied on cara-4 avatars (avatarModel `cara-4` or `cara-4-latest`); if set on a cara-3 avatar they are ignored (silently stripped) and the session proceeds without them. `presetStyle` and `customStylePrompt` are mutually exclusive. These work best when the selected voice matches the intended performance.

presetStyle.description: Built-in performance style for the avatar to follow. Mutually exclusive with customStylePrompt. Works best with a matching voice, which we've labelled as expressive.

customStylePrompt.description: Free-form performance style prompt for the avatar to follow. Mutually exclusive with presetStyle. Works best with a matching voice, which we've labelled as expressive.
customStylePrompt.example: Warm smile, composed, slightly amused, looking directly at camera

expressivity.description: Controls how closely the avatar follows the selected style or cue. 0 is subtle, 1 follows it most strongly and can become unstable; omit the field to use the default. Works best with a matching voice, which we've labelled as expressive.

tools.description: Runtime tool definitions made available to the persona for this session. Each item is one of a client tool, a server knowledge tool, a server webhook tool, or a system tool. For client and webhook tools, `parameters` (and, for webhook tools, `queryParameters`) is a JSON Schema object the LLM fills at call time; each such object must serialize to 10,000 bytes or less (UTF-8), otherwise the request is rejected. Use `toolIds` instead to reference tools you've pre-created via `/v1/tools` (those are not subject to this inline size limit).

type.description: Tool kind. `server` tools additionally set `subtype` (`knowledge` or `webhook`).

subtype.description: Required when `type` is `server`. `knowledge` searches documents in `config.documentFolderIds` (`rag` is a legacy alias for `knowledge`, kept for backwards compatibility); `webhook` calls an external URL.

name.description: Unique tool name the LLM calls.

config.description: Type-specific configuration for a `knowledge` server tool.

documentFolderIds.description: IDs of knowledge folders to search.

topK.description: Nested form of the flat `topK` field. The flat value is used when both are set.

minScore.description: Nested form of the flat `minScore` field. The flat value is used when both are set.

maxContextTokens.description: Nested form of the flat `maxContextTokens` field. The flat value is used when both are set.

neighborChunks.description: Nested form of the flat `neighborChunks` field. The flat value is used when both are set.

documentFolderIds.description: Legacy flat form of `config.documentFolderIds`, kept for backwards compatibility. If both are set, this flat value is used.

topK.description: Knowledge tools only. Maximum matching chunks to retrieve. Overrides the engine default. Omit or set null to use the default. Fixed tool configuration, not an LLM argument.

minScore.description: Knowledge tools only. Minimum relevance score for retrieved chunks. Zero is valid. Omit or set null to use the default. Fixed tool configuration, not an LLM argument.

maxContextTokens.description: Knowledge tools only. Retrieved content token budget, excluding metadata and prompt formatting. Omit or set null to use the default. Fixed tool configuration, not an LLM argument.

neighborChunks.description: Knowledge tools only. Chunks to add after each match, plus the chunk before it, for surrounding context. 0 returns matches only. Defaults to 0 when omitted or null. Fixed tool configuration, not an LLM argument.

parameters.description: JSON Schema for the arguments the LLM provides (client and webhook tools). Must serialize to 10,000 bytes or less.

example.name: open_calendar
example.description: Open the calendar UI in the client app.

date.description: Date to jump to, in YYYY-MM-DD format.

example.name: search_docs
example.description: Search the knowledge base for relevant documents.

toolIds.description: IDs of tools pre-created via `/v1/tools` to make available to the persona for this session.

oneOf.description: Avatar-only rendering with audio supplied by the client.

enableAudioPassthrough.description: Must be true; the client supplies audio for the avatar.

voiceGenerationOptions.description: Only `pronunciationDictionaryId` applies to a saved persona; voice settings come from the persona, and any other keys are ignored.

environment.description: Optional engine routing or transport integration environment. The integration type may be supplied explicitly or inferred from the LiveKit, Agora, or ElevenLabs Agent settings.

livekitUrl.description: Must be reachable from the public internet; loopback, private, link-local, reserved, documentation, cluster-internal, and single-label targets are rejected with HTTP 400. Use an absolute URL with an ASCII hostname (punycode for international names), canonical dotted-decimal IPv4, and a port from 1 to 65535 if specified. Hostnames must resolve only to public addresses; DNS is checked when the session starts. Temporary DNS failures are service errors (5xx), not invalid URL errors.

oneOf.description: Default Anam WebRTC transport with optional engine routing.

sessionReplay.description: Legacy control for both the recording and the transcript. Use dataRetention instead. It can be sent alongside dataRetention: enableSessionReplay false turns both off, and so does an empty sessionReplay object; enableSessionReplay true leaves each to dataRetention.

enableSessionReplay.description: Record the session and store its transcript. false turns off both, the same as dataRetention with recording and transcripts set to false. Under Zero Data Retention, sending true without dataRetention returns HTTP 400; with dataRetention sent, omitted settings are off and only a dataRetention setting of true that this flag (false, or an empty sessionReplay) does not turn off is rejected.

dataRetention.description: Choose what Anam keeps after the session. Each setting is independent, so you can turn off the recording and keep the transcript, or the other way round. A sessionReplay sent alongside it with enableSessionReplay false, or with no value, turns both off. Zero Data Retention sessions keep neither: an omitted setting is off, and a setting of true returns HTTP 400 unless sessionReplay turns both off. Not supported for LiveKit or Agora sessions (HTTP 400).

recording.description: Record the session video. When false, GET /v1/sessions/{id}/recording returns 404. With sessionOptions.egress mode daily the recording must resolve to off: set this to false, or set enableSessionReplay to false or send an empty sessionReplay.

transcripts.description: Store the conversation transcript. When false, GET /v1/sessions/{id}/transcript returns transcriptsEnabled false and each message reads TRANSCRIPTS_DISABLED.

videoQuality.description: 'high' pins highest bitrate, 'auto' enables adaptive bitrate.

showAIAvatarDisclosure.description: Show the AI avatar disclosure during the session. Defaults to false; set true to opt in. Agora sessions ignore this field.

region.description: Requested engine region. This explicit choice is honored independently of automatic geographic routing.

regionPolicy.description: `preferred` allows cross-region capacity failover. `strict` keeps the session in the requested region and requires `region`.

videoWidth.description: Output video frame width in pixels. Supply together with `videoHeight` (both or neither). Omit to use the avatar model's default. Supported pairs depend on the avatar model — cara-3: `720x480`; cara-4: `1152x768`. Unsupported pairs are rejected (the session is not silently downgraded).

videoHeight.description: Output video frame height in pixels. Supply together with `videoWidth` (both or neither). See `videoWidth`.

egress.description:
Set egress to an alternative egress transport mode. The avatar's audio/video are published to
a 3rd party transport and not delivered over the native webRTC channel.
The WebRTC peer connection still exists for signalling and the data channel (interrupts, status).
Requires `personaConfig.enableAudioPassthrough=true`. Discriminated on `mode`.

mode.description: Egress provider. Only `daily` is supported today.

roomUrl.description: Daily room URL the avatar should join as a publisher.

token.description: Optional Daily meeting token. Omit for public rooms.

userName.description: Optional display name for the avatar participant. Defaults to "anam-avatar".

400.description: Invalid request body or incompatible Zero Data Retention configuration. ZDR requests are rejected when the selected voice, LLM or STT provider does not support ZDR, compatibility cannot be verified, dataRetention.recording or dataRetention.transcripts is set to true without a sessionReplay that turns both off, or sessionReplay.enableSessionReplay is set to true without dataRetention. Omitted dataRetention settings are off for ZDR sessions. Region values must be `eu` or `us`, and `regionPolicy: strict` requires an explicit `region`. Avatar-only persona configs (avatarId without voiceId and without enableAudioPassthrough: true) are rejected with `avatar_only_requires_integration` unless a LiveKit, Agora or ElevenLabs Agent integration `environment` is supplied.

post.description:
Start a live persona session.

Two authentication modes are supported via the `Authorization: Bearer` header:

- **Session token** (browser clients): pass a session token minted by `POST /v1/auth/session-token`.
  The session configuration was bound to the token when it was created, so the body only carries
  optional `clientMetadata`. This is the flow the client-side SDKs use; you normally don't call
  this endpoint yourself.
- **API key** (server-side SDKs): pass your API key directly and supply the session configuration
  in the request body — the same shape as the `/v1/auth/session-token` body (`personaConfig`,
  `environment`, `sessionOptions`, plus optional `clientLabel` and `clientMetadata`; `expiresIn`
  and `widgetConfig` do not apply). This skips the session-token exchange. Only use this from a
  secure server-side context — never expose an API key in a browser.

clientLabel.description: Label for the session, recorded for usage attribution. API-key auth only.

personaConfig.description:
Session persona configuration (API-key auth only). Same shape as the
`/v1/auth/session-token` request: supply `personaId` for a persona you've already
created, or `avatarId`/`voiceId`/`llmId`/`systemPrompt` for an ephemeral persona.
An avatar-only config (avatarId without voiceId and without
enableAudioPassthrough: true) is only accepted together with a LiveKit,
Agora or ElevenLabs Agent integration `environment`; on the default Anam
WebRTC transport send an ephemeral config with voiceId and llmId (llmId
"CUSTOMER_CLIENT_V1" for a client-side LLM) or set
enableAudioPassthrough to true. Otherwise the request fails
with 400 `avatar_only_requires_integration`.
Knowledge tools accept optional fixed `topK` (integer 1–100), `minScore`
(number 0–1), `maxContextTokens` (integer 1–200,000; content only) and
`neighborChunks` (integer 0–10, default 0) on each tool. Omit or set null to retain defaults. Invalid values return 400.
Inline `tools` are supported; each client/webhook tool's `parameters` (and webhook
`queryParameters`) JSON Schema must serialize to 10,000 bytes or less (UTF-8).
`voiceGenerationOptions.pronunciationDictionaryId` selects a pronunciation
dictionary for the session (see `SessionPronunciationDictionary`); its latest
saved entries are applied when the session starts.

environment.description: Optional environment configuration (e.g. LiveKit settings). API-key auth only.

livekitUrl.description: Must be reachable from the public internet; loopback, private, link-local, reserved, documentation, cluster-internal, and single-label targets are rejected with HTTP 400. Use an absolute URL with an ASCII hostname (punycode for international names), canonical dotted-decimal IPv4, and a port from 1 to 65535 if specified. Hostnames must resolve only to public addresses; DNS is checked when the session starts. Temporary DNS failures are service errors (5xx), not invalid URL errors.

sessionOptions.description: Optional session options for API-key-authenticated session creation, including data retention (recording and transcripts), video quality/dimensions, AI avatar disclosure, egress, and engine-region routing. For session-token authentication, configure these options when creating the token.

sessionReplay.description: Legacy control for both the recording and the transcript. Use dataRetention instead. It can be sent alongside dataRetention: enableSessionReplay false turns both off, and so does an empty sessionReplay object; enableSessionReplay true leaves each to dataRetention.

enableSessionReplay.description: Record the session and store its transcript. false turns off both, the same as dataRetention with recording and transcripts set to false. Under Zero Data Retention, sending true without dataRetention returns HTTP 400; with dataRetention sent, omitted settings are off and only a dataRetention setting of true that this flag (false, or an empty sessionReplay) does not turn off is rejected.

dataRetention.description: Choose what Anam keeps after the session. Each setting is independent, so you can turn off the recording and keep the transcript, or the other way round. A sessionReplay sent alongside it with enableSessionReplay false, or with no value, turns both off. Zero Data Retention sessions keep neither: an omitted setting is off, and a setting of true returns HTTP 400 unless sessionReplay turns both off. Not supported for LiveKit or Agora sessions (HTTP 400).

recording.description: Record the session video. When false, GET /v1/sessions/{id}/recording returns 404. With sessionOptions.egress mode daily the recording must resolve to off: set this to false, or set enableSessionReplay to false or send an empty sessionReplay.

transcripts.description: Store the conversation transcript. When false, GET /v1/sessions/{id}/transcript returns transcriptsEnabled false and each message reads TRANSCRIPTS_DISABLED.

videoQuality.description: 'high' pins highest bitrate, 'auto' enables adaptive bitrate.

showAIAvatarDisclosure.description: Show the AI avatar disclosure during the session. Defaults to false; set true to opt in. Agora sessions ignore this field.

region.description: Requested engine region. Explicit selection works even when automatic geographic routing is disabled.

regionPolicy.description: `preferred` allows cross-region capacity failover. `strict` requires `region` and never serves the session from another region.

videoWidth.description: Output video frame width in pixels. Supply together with `videoHeight` (both or neither). Omit to use the avatar model's default. Supported pairs depend on the avatar model — cara-3: `720x480`; cara-4: `1152x768`. Unsupported pairs are rejected (the session is not silently downgraded).

videoHeight.description: Output video frame height in pixels. Supply together with `videoWidth` (both or neither). See `videoWidth`.

egress.description:
Set egress to an alternative egress transport mode. The avatar's audio/video are published to
a 3rd party transport and not delivered over the native webRTC channel.
The WebRTC peer connection still exists for signalling and the data channel (interrupts, status).
Requires `personaConfig.enableAudioPassthrough=true`. Discriminated on `mode`.

mode.description: Egress provider. Only `daily` is supported today.

roomUrl.description: Daily room URL the avatar should join as a publisher.

token.description: Optional Daily meeting token. Omit for public rooms.

userName.description: Optional display name for the avatar participant. Defaults to "anam-avatar".

clientMetadata.description: Optional client metadata forwarded to the engine (e.g. supportsPubSubSignalling).

engineHost.description: Host of the engine serving this session. Omitted for LiveKit/Agora integrations.

region.description: Actual region that served the session. Omitted when the serving session-service does not report it.

400.description: Invalid request body or persona configuration, including a ZDR request whose selected voice or LLM is incompatible, whose compatibility cannot be verified, that sets dataRetention.recording or dataRetention.transcripts to true without a sessionReplay that turns both off, or that sets sessionReplay.enableSessionReplay to true without dataRetention. Omitted dataRetention settings are off for ZDR sessions. Region values must be `eu` or `us`, and `regionPolicy: strict` requires an explicit `region`. Avatar-only persona configs (avatarId without voiceId and without enableAudioPassthrough: true) are rejected with `avatar_only_requires_integration` unless a LiveKit, Agora or ElevenLabs Agent integration `environment` is supplied. An avatar with no engine key (one created without an image) is rejected with `avatar_unusable`. Deleting that avatar is not enough on its own: deletion is a soft delete, a replacement created with `imageUrl` gets a new `avatarId`, and saved personas keep referencing the old one. Point the session config or saved persona at a usable `avatarId` instead. If the engine rejects the session configuration, the error is `invalid_session_config`, with the rejected field names in `invalid_fields` when the engine reports them.

mcp.description:
Start a live persona session.

Two authentication modes are supported via the `Authorization: Bearer` header:

- **Session token** (browser clients): pass a session token minted by `POST /v1/auth/session-token`.
  The session configuration was bound to the token when it was created, so the body only carries
  optional `clientMetadata`. This is the flow the client-side SDKs use; you normally don't call
  this endpoint yourself.
- **API key** (server-side SDKs): pass your API key directly and supply the session configuration
  in the request body — the same shape as the `/v1/auth/session-token` body (`personaConfig`,
  `environment`, `sessionOptions`, plus optional `clientLabel` and `clientMetadata`; `expiresIn`
  and `widgetConfig` do not apply). This skips the session-token exchange. Only use this from a
  secure server-side context — never expose an API key in a browser.

delete.description: Delete an avatar by ID. By default this is a soft delete: the avatar is hidden and can be restored. Pass `hard=true` to permanently purge the avatar and its stored assets (source image and generated versions). A hard delete cannot be undone and is intended for data-erasure requests; it also purges avatars that were previously soft-deleted. A hard delete never deletes personas: when active personas (or their drafts) still use the avatar the request fails with `409 Conflict` and the impacted persona IDs.
